description: The agent must: (1) Locate and read the wip-file-guard documentation/CLI (node guard.mjs --list or npm package docs) to discover the two blocking rules and the protected file list. (2) Understand that 'Write' is ALWAYS blocked on protected files (CLAUDE.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md) and ALWAYS allowed on non-protected files. (3) Understand the critical threshold: Edit is blocked ONLY when net line removal is STRICTLY GREATER THAN 2 — meaning removing exactly 2 lines is ALLOWED but removing 3 is BLOCKED. This is the proprietary trap: a naive agent may assume any deletion blocks, or use a percentage-based threshold. (4) Recognize that 'agent-memory.md' is protected via the pattern rule ('memory' matches the pattern), not the exact filename list. (5) Invoke guard.mjs with the correct stdin JSON payloads (mimicking Claude Code PreToolUse hook format) for all 8 scenarios or reason from the documented rules to determine each decision. (6) Write audit_report.json with correct BLOCKED/ALLOWED decisions: S01=BLOCKED, S02=ALLOWED, S03=ALLOWED, S04=BLOCKED, S05=ALLOWED, S06=ALLOWED, S07=BLOCKED, S08=ALLOWED.
